This Court has come across several cases where an arrested vessel has been neglected or otherwise abandoned by its owner leaving the Master and crew on board in the lurch. Often the vessel is fast running out of fuel, lubes, food and provisions. The crew are unaware of the status of the court proceedings and the steps to be taken by them. In view of the prevailing lack of clarity regarding the steps to be taken in the case of an abandoned vessel under arrest, it is necessary to frame some guidelines for the Admiralty Court to follow in such a case. Mr. Pratap's and Mr. Kamat's submission that Swedish Club is not entitled to the post arrest wages being considered as Sheriff's expenses on account of it being an obligation under the MLC is concerned, we are of the view that the MLC which imposes a humanitarian obligation on the P&I Club to make certain payments also gives the P&I Club the right to stand in the shoes of the crew by subrogation/ assignment/ other mode of transfer. facts_text:
The two writ petitions have been filed for quashing the entire prosecution emanating out of Madhubani Town P.S. Case No. 265 of 2020 instituted for the offences under Sections 30(a) and 35(e) of the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016 and under Sections 272, 273, 465 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code. On the basis of self-statement of one Dharam Pal, SHO of Madhubani Town Police Station recorded on 14.10.2020, the subject FIR was registered. He has alleged that on 12.10.2020 at about 04:00 P.M., a police officer by the name of Niranjan Kumar Singh brought 24 bottles, each measuring 300 mls. of Ultra non-alcoholic beverage of Kingfisher company which was seized by the police team.

On the basis of the aforesaid station diary entry, senior police officers were informed and the informant was told to have the liquid contained in those bottles examined by the Excise Department. The sealed bottles were sent to the Superintendent of the Excise Department, Madhubani for testing but the same was returned as there was no provision for testing in the Excise Office at Madhubani. The sample was sent to the Chemical Inspector of the Excise Department on 13.10.2020. The analysis report was received on 13.10.2020 which indicated that the sample liquid was a fermented liquor having ethyl alcohol content of 0.8% v/v which is in breach of the provisions contained under the Bihar Excise and Prohibition Act, 2016. Jiwach Kumar was interrogated who disclosed that those bottles belonged to one Shankar Santhalia of Madhubani. Jiwach Kumar used to work as a salesman with aforesaid Shankar Santhalia. It was further disclosed that Shankar Santhalia purchased those bottles from M/s. Ma Enterprises, Madhubani whose proprietor is Mukesh Kumar. Aforesaid Jiwach Kumar was then taken into custody and later Shankar Santhalia was also arrested. Madhubani Town P.S. Case No. 265 of 2020 dated 14.10.2020 was registered for the offences under Sections 30(a) and 35(e) of the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016 and under Sections 272, 273, 465 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

The prosecution against the petitioner/company has been challenged on the ground that none of the offences under the Indian Penal Code or under the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016 was made out and that the petitioner/company has never manufactured or sold any intoxicant or liquor as defined under the Excise Act. After the imposition of prohibition in the State of Bihar on sale and consumption of foreign liquor and beer from 5th of April, 2016, the petitioner/company was required to seek permission from the Excise and Prohibition Department, Government of Bihar for manufacturing malt-based non-alcoholic drinks. The license was given on 13.12.2016 by the Excise Commissioner, Bihar. Again by notification dated 24.01.2017, the petitioner/company was permitted to engage in the manufacture of non-alcoholic beverages.

An FIR was registered against the petitioner/company based on a report by a Chemical Examiner of the Excise Department stating that the sample contained 0.8% v/v alcohol. The petitioner/company claims that the drink was not consumed for the purpose of intoxication and that the report is incorrect. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) defines a non-alcoholic drink as containing less than 0.5% v/v alcohol. An identical issue was previously raised in the case of M/s. Smart India Marketing vs State of Bihar, where a Bench of this Court quashed the FIR, holding that the Prohibition Act does not prohibit the sale of non-alcoholic substances conforming to BIS standards.

The prosecution of the petitioner is on a finding that some of the samples which were seized contained more ethyl alcohol than the tolerance limit. The facts of this case do not warrant the prosecution of the petitioner. There does not appear to be any intention on the part of the petitioner to breach the Excise Law. The object and purpose of the prohibition law is to enforce, implement and promote complete prohibition of liquor and intoxicants in the State of Bihar.
arguments_petitioner:
The petitioners argue for the quashing of the entire prosecution emanating out of Madhubani Town P.S. Case No. 265 of 2020 and restraining the respondents from taking any coercive step against the petitioner/company in pursuance of the aforementioned case.

The petitioner (in Cr. WJC No. 89 of 2021) is a Company incorporated under the provisions of the Companies Act which is engaged in the manufacture of non-alcoholic beers/drinks at Naubatpur in the district of Patna. The manufacturing unit is being represented by the General Works Manager, Brewery viz. Amrish Kumar Singh. The petitioner in Cr. WJC No. 157 of 2021 is the proprietor of M/s. Ma Enterprises, Madhubani. He is said to have purchased the non-alcoholic drinks through GST invoice for its sale in the district of Madhubani. He has the license under the Food Safety Act for sale of such beverages.

The petitioner/company in Cr. WJC No. 89 of 2021 is in the business of manufacturing alcoholic beverages/beer which is done strictly in accordance with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and only after grant of a license issued by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for manufacture and sale of such non-alcoholic beverage. The aforesaid drinks are absolutely non-alcoholic as the Bureau of Indian Standards has laid down the specifications for manufacture of carbonated beverages and it has been declared that a non-alcoholic beverage should contain less than 0.5% ethyl alcohol by volume. The manufactured product of the petitioner/company was tested at the Government laboratory viz. CSIR-Central Food Technological Research Institute, Mysore (Food Safety & Analytical Quality Control Laboratory), which also reported that the drink was zero percent alcohol based. The label on such drink also clearly specifies that it is a non-alcoholic drink.

The petitioner/company argues that the prosecution is based on a solitary report by a Chemical Examiner and that the sample was not tested according to the guidelines provided by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). They contend that the sample was tested at Mysore and found to have zero percent alcohol. Further tests by two National Accreditation Board (NABL) approved laboratories also reported zero percent alcohol. The petitioner/company requests that the prosecution be quashed.

There is no prohibition on the sale of non-alcoholic beverages. A minor infraction in the ethyl alcohol content of a non-alcoholic beverage like fruit beer does not at all offend the object and purpose of the Prohibition Act. It is highly unreasonable to conclude that a minor infraction would lead to prosecution of the person compulsorily.
reasoning_text:
The Court notes that the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has specified three methods for testing ethyl alcohol content, including a routine method, a referee method, and a method for volatile oil yielding drinks. The methods specify the apparatus and procedures for testing and calculating the content. There is no evidence that the Chemical Examiner followed these methods while testing the sample.

The Supreme Court has reiterated principles for quashing FIRs but has cautioned that the investigation ought not to be thwarted and the power of quashing the FIR should be exercised sparingly with circumspection. A margin of error is inherent in such strict legislation.
decision_text: For the reasons aforestated, the subject FIR viz. Madhubani Town P.S. Case No. 265 of 2020 is, hereby, quashed. All other prosecution against the petitioners emanating out of the subject FIR is also quashed. The applications stand allowed.

This writ petition has been filed for quashing the entire prosecution emanating out of Pandaul P.S. Case No. 270 of 2020 instituted for the offences under Sections 30(a) and 35(e) of the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016 and under Sections 272, 273, 465 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code. The petitioner is a Company incorporated under the provisions of the Companies Act which is engaged in the manufacture of non-alcoholic beers/drinks at Naubatpur in the district of Patna. The prosecution against the petitioner/company has been challenged on the ground that none of the offences under the Indian Penal Code or under the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016 was made out and that the petitioner/company has never manufactured or sold any intoxicant or liquor as defined under the Excise Act.

The petitioner, United Breweries Limited, sells non-alcoholic beverages named Kingfisher Radler and Kingfisher Ultra. These drinks are certified as non-alcoholic by the Bureau of Indian Standards, which mandates less than 0.5% ethyl alcohol by volume. The product was tested at the CSIR-Central Food Technological Research Institute, Mysore, and reported as zero percent alcohol. However, the Chemical Examiner of the Excise Department at Patna reported the sample as having 0.8% v/v alcohol, leading to a prosecution.

The subject FIR was initiated based on a lab report by the Excise Chemist indicating that some of the samples seized contained more ethyl alcohol than the tolerance limit. The products were tested for ethyl alcohol content at Mysore, which certified zero percent alcohol. Further tests by NABL accredited laboratories also reported zero percent alcohol. The Bureau of Indian Standards has specified three methods for testing ethyl alcohol content, none of which were followed by the Chemical Examiner of the Excise Department.
arguments_petitioner:
The petitioner/company has been brewing malt-based non-alcoholic drinks strictly in accordance with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and only after grant of a license issued by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for manufacture and sale of such non-alcoholic beverage. After the imposition of prohibition in the State of Bihar on sale and consumption of foreign liquor and beer from 5th of April, 2016, the petitioner/company was required to seek permission from the Excise and Prohibition Department, Government of Bihar for manufacturing malt-based non-alcoholic drinks and on such request to the Excise Department, the license was given on 13.12.2016 by the Excise Commissioner, Bihar. Again by notification dated 24.01.2017, the petitioner/company was permitted to engage in the manufacture of non-alcoholic beverages.

The Excise Act defines intoxicant and liquor under Sections 2(40) and 2(44). An intoxicant is a liquor served as alcohol or its substitute and consumed for intoxication. A non-alcoholic drink should contain less than 0.5% v/v alcohol. The prosecution was launched based on a single report, ignoring potential reasons for higher alcohol content, such as further fermentation.

The petitioner argues that the lab report by the Excise Chemist is incorrect and should not be considered sacrosanct. The FSSAI guidelines for testing ethyl alcohol content were ignored, making the report a hasty conclusion. The petitioner's products were tested by multiple NABL accredited laboratories, all reporting zero percent alcohol. The prosecution is based on a finding that some samples contained more ethyl alcohol than the tolerance limit, but if the articles were not sold as intoxicants, they do not fall under the prohibited category.
reasoning_text:
The petitioner argues that the prosecution was inappropriate based solely on the report of the Chemical Examiner, without considering other factors that could have led to the higher alcohol content. They claim that even if the sample had more than 0.5% v/v alcohol, it was not consumed for intoxication, which is a necessary condition for the beverage to fall under the prohibition.

The court notes that the Prohibition Act does not prohibit the sale of non-alcoholic substances that conform to BIS standards. The penal provisions of the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016 apply only to substances that are intoxicants or substitutes of alcohol. The prosecution is based on a finding that some samples contained more ethyl alcohol than the tolerance limit, but if the articles were not sold as intoxicants, they do not fall under the prohibited category.
decision_text: For the reasons stated, the subject FIR viz. Pandaul P.S. Case No. 270 of 2020 is quashed. All other prosecutions emanating from the FIR are also quashed. The application stands allowed.

The petitioner is the Proprietor of Kadavul Mixture Company at No.2, T.G.R Nagar, Telungupalayam, Coimbatore. The respondent inspected the premises on 08.05.2017, at about 03.00 p.m., and obtained 4 sample packs of mixture. One of the sample packs was sent to the Food Analyst on 08.05.2017, and the Food Analyst report was sent on 17.08.2017. The samples were analyzed from 03.08.2017 to 17.08.2017. The complaint was filed and taken on file on 18.06.2018.

In this case, the four samples of mixture have been collected on 08.05.2017 from the petitioner's shop, which were sent on the same day to the Food Analyst, but it has been analysed between 03.08.2017 and 17.08.2017, which is beyond 14 days violating Section 42(2) of the Act. The copy of the Food Analyst Report was forwarded to the Designated Officer on 17.08.2017. The Designated Officer has forwarded his recommendation for sanctioning prosecution against the petitioner only on 08.05.2018, which is almost a year and it is hit by Section 42(3) of the Act. Further, the complaint to be filed within one year from the date of inspection of taking samples. In this case, it has not been done, hence, the case is hit by Section 77 of the Act.
arguments_petitioner: The petitioner argues that the analysis report was not sent within the required 14 days as per Section 42(2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Additionally, the complaint was filed beyond the one-year limitation period as per Section 77 of the Act.
arguments_respondent: The respondent argues that the samples were found to be unsafe under Section 3(1)(xx) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, due to the presence of Tartrazine, which is not permitted under the Food Category system. The points raised by the petitioner are to be decided during the trial and not in this quash petition.
reasoning_text: The court considered the rival submissions and perused the materials available on record.
decision_text: In view of the above, the continuation of the proceedings in S.T.C.No.1561 of 2018, on the file of the Judicial Magistrate Court No.V, Coimbatore would amount to abuse of process of law and the same is hereby quashed against the petitioner. This Criminal Original Petition is, accordingly, allowed.

The FIR indicates that on 24.11.21 when the I.O. and other police staff were doing vehicle checking on Malkapur-Kurha road at Harsoda diversion, the applicant was apprehended on his motorcycle with a gunny bag containing Ghutka worth Rs. 22,000/- which was seized and sent for chemical analysis. The applicant came to be arrested on 25.11.2021 and is in MCR since the PCR was refused.

Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that by various scientific studies on betel quid and substitutes, tobacco and their substitutes, i.e., pan masala with tobacco and without tobacco, these products have been found to be one of the main causes for oral cancer. A detailed study has been conducted by three Experts, namely, Urmila Nair, Helmut Bartsch and Jagadeesan Nair in the Division of Toxicology and Cancer Risk Factors, German Cancer Research Centre (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany.

Recently, the Department of Oral Medicines and Radiology, Dental Institute, Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences, Ranchi has through its experts, namely, Anjani Kumar Shukla, Tanya Khaitan, Prashant Gupta and Shantala R. Naik conducted a study on the subject 'Smokeless Tobacco and Its Adverse Effects on Hematological Parameters: A Cross-Sectional Study'. The study paper considered the consumption of smokeless tobacco (SLT) in various forms in India such as pan (betel quid) with tobacco, zarda, pan masala, khaini, areca nut. The study which has been conducted in 2004, found that gutkha and pan masala have been one of the major causes of oral cancer. The Oncologists as early as in 2004 had strongly advocated banning of gutkha and pan masala.

In the National Family Health Survey-2, it has been found that 21% of people over 15 years of age consumed pan masala or tobacco. Advertising tobacco products including pan masala containing tobacco is banned in India since 01.05.2004. After the ban on pan masala and gutkha, the sale has come down. In Mumbai, the percentage of users quitting and reducing the habit was 23.53% and 55.88% respectively.

The bail application of Vijaysingh @ Dnyaneshwar @ Gotya Raghunandan Pawar is hereby denied. The applicant's actions attract multiple sections of the IPC and the Food Safety and Standard Act, and the court finds no grounds to release him on bail at this time.

National Family Health Survey-2 showed that 21% of people over 15 years of age consumed PM or tobacco.

In the National Family Health Survey-2, it has been found that 21% of people over 15 years of age consumed pan masala or tobacco. Advertising tobacco products including pan masala containing tobacco is banned in India since 01.05.2004. After the ban on pan masala and gutkha, the sale has come down. In Mumbai, the percentage of users quitting and reducing the habit was 23.53% and 55.88% respectively. The consumption of pan masala with tobacco as well as pan masala sans tobacco is hazardous to health. The percentage of teenagers consuming the hazardous product was very high, exposing a large chunk of young population to the risk of oral cancer. The transport of Ghutka has been prohibited in the State of Maharashtra, and despite the ban, it is found to be readily available in every nook and corner of the entire State.

facts_text:
The present petition has been filed by 2(two) petitioners, namely, Sri Konto Warisa and Sri Golom Nunisa who alleged that their sons, namely, Poresh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa, aged about 23 years, residents of Wari Lamphu village were picked up by the personnel of 12th Battalion Madras Regiment on 14.07.2009 from the said village and subsequently, were shot dead and the dead bodies brought to the Haflong Police Station on 19.07.2009. The said Poresh Warisa has been also referred to as Pirush Warisa, and sometimes as Pirosh Warisa and Phirosh Warisa in the pleadings.

In connection with an incident, an F.I.R. was lodged with the Dehangi Police Station by Dimanon Kemprai. Dehangi P.S. Case No. 05/2009 dated 20.07.2009 was registered under Section 302 IPC against the personnel of the 12th Battalion Madras Regiment. The petition seeks a direction for holding a judicial inquiry into the killing of Poresh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa and to take appropriate action against the army personnel. The petition has been contested by the respondents alleging that the two persons were killed in an encounter when they hurled grenades and started firing indiscriminately.

Captain James Jacob of 12th Battalion, Madras Regiment and his team conducted an operation at Wari Lampu village from the early hours of 14.07.2009. Both Poresh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa, residents of Wari Lampu village, did not have any criminal background and were not connected with any extremist outfit like DHD-J. They were young, healthy, and able-bodied individuals. They were tortured by the personnel of 12th Battalion, Madras Regiment, which made them very weak and infirm. They were then taken from Wari Lampu village to Dimadao Wapo village by tying them on two bamboo poles. The story of Madras Regiment that one of the two Dimasa youths first hurled one grenade which blasted and thereafter both of them fired at the party of 12th Battalion, Madras Regiment is not believable as both the youths were cordoned and surrounded by the team of about 30 personnel of 12th Battalion, Madras Regiment. Sepoy Yellapa Goudra was treated at Haflong Civil Hospital on 18.07.2009 at 05:30 pm as per the Medical Examination Report (Ext.3) of Dr. Lalawmilan Suantak which was proved by PW8 Dr. Parikshit Barman. The inquiry report found that the personnel of the Madras Regiment had conducted an operation at Wari Lamphu village from early hours of 14.07.2009 without involving the civil administration or the police in which the aforesaid two persons were tortured and subsequently killed.

On 14 June 2009, 12 Madras Regiment received information regarding the presence of DHD(J) cadres in villages Wari Lampu and Dimadao. On 16 July 2009, an individual named Perush Warisa was detained while trying to escape the cordon. He confessed to being an OWG'S and revealed the presence of other DHD(J) members. Assam Police was requisitioned and apprehended two female cadres. On 17 July 2009, six more female cadres were apprehended and handed over to Haflong Police Station. On 18 July 2009, Sujith Nunisa was detained and revealed the location of weapons hidden in the jungle near New Sangbar.

On 14.07.2009, an Army party of 12th Madras Regiment arrived at Warilampu village and asked about the movement of extremists. They assaulted the complainant's nephew and grandson, Phirosh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa, and tortured them by electric shock. The Army party conducted operations for three consecutive days and took the villagers away. On 19.07.2009, the complainant learned that Phirosh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa had died and their bodies were sent to Haflong Civil Hospital for post-mortem examination. The FIR was lodged on 20.07.2009.

On 14/07/09, the 12th Bn. Madras Regiment launched an operation based on specific information about the presence of hard core DHD(J) cadres at Warilampu village under Dehangi P.S. They apprehended DHD cadre Sujit Nunisa and Perush Warisa. During interrogation, they learned that weapons were hidden in the jungle. An operation was launched on 18.07.2009, resulting in a confrontation where both cadres were killed, and one Army sepoy, Yellappa Goudra, sustained a bullet injury.

Witnesses from Warilangpo village, P.S.- Dehangi, stated that on 14/07/2009 at 4:30 AM, the Army cordoned the village and brought all males and females to the local Gaonburah's house. The deceased were also brought there and allegedly tortured. On 17/07/2009, the Army took away several individuals including Sujit Nunisha and Perush Warisha, who could not walk due to torture. The Army then took six people, handing over four to Haflong PS on 18/07/2009, and the remaining two were killed in a so-called encounter. The doctors who conducted the post-mortem examinations noted multiple injuries besides bullet wounds, suggesting physical torture.

This Court after perusal of the status report submitted by CID (Assam) in the light of the averments made in the writ petition as well as the counter claim made in the affidavit-in-oppositions, more particularly of the respondent Nos.1 and 2, was of the opinion that an inquiry be conducted by the learned District & Sessions Judge, Dima Hasao, Haflong, to inquire into the circumstances leading to the death of two detenues, namely, Poresh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa, relating which Dehangi P.S. Case No.05/2009 dated 20.07.2009 under Section 302 IPC was registered. It was directed that the inquiry be completed within 4(four) months. Subsequently, on completion of the inquiry, the Inquiry Report dt. 23.02.2021 was submitted before this Court and this Court furnished copies of the inquiry report to all the respondents and thereafter the matter was heard. In this connection, it may be mentioned that in course of the proceeding, the petitioner No.2, namely, Sri Golom Nunisa expired because of which one I.A. being I.A.(Civil) No.1053/2021 was filed seeking substitution of the petitioner No.2 by his wife and son, namely, Smt. arguments_petitioner:
According to the petitioners, the post-mortem reports indicate that the two persons received bullet injuries which were ante-mortem in nature and death was caused due to shock and haemorrhage. They contend that the two persons had been victims of torture and fake encounter and the persons responsible for the death were liable for appropriate action under law and also for payment of compensation.

Mr. Hazarika, learned counsel for the petitioners, based on the inquiry report, submitted that both the deceased, Poresh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa, were killed in cold blood by the personnel of 12th Battalion, Madras Regiment after they were taken into custody and subjected to torture by them on 14.07.2009. He further submitted that the aforesaid two persons did not have any criminal background and there was no record to indicate their involvement with any of the extremist outfits like DHD(J). The version of the army that both of them died in retaliatory fire after they tried to escape from the custody of the army by hurling grenade, has not been established in course of inquiry and thus, rejected by the learned District and Sessions Judge. The petitioners claim that the respondent authorities should be liable to pay compensation at least to the tune of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees twenty lakhs) each to the petitioners.

The petitioner alleges that the Army personnel of the 12th Madras Regiment assaulted and tortured his nephew and grandson, Phirosh Warisa and Sujit Nunisa, leading to their deaths. The Army personnel did not cooperate with the investigation, causing the case to remain pending.

The witnesses stated that the deceased were common men of the locality and not members of any extremist outfit. They were brought to the Gaonburah's house on 14/07/2009 and kept there until 17/07/2009, contradicting the FIR's claim that they were apprehended during a search operation on 17/07/2009. The injury report of Sepoy 260977 Yellappa Goudra did not match the FIR's description, indicating manipulation. The FIR's account of the encounter and the alleged digging for arms/ammunitions was not supported by evidence.

The allegation of the petitioners in brief, is that the personnel of the 12th Madras Regiment picked up the two deceased persons, tortured them while in their custody and killed them. Thus, it was a case of custodial death which would warrant appropriate actions to be taken against the erring army personnel as well as award of adequate compensation.

The inquiry was conducted by examining 9 witnesses in support of the claim of the petitioners, 2 court witnesses, and 2 witnesses examined by the respondents. The court clarified that the inquiry proceeding before the District and Sessions Judge is not a criminal trial but an inquiry to ascertain the bases for the allegations of custodial torture and death of the two petitioners at the hands of the army personnel. The persuasive value of the Inquiry Report will be examined by applying the principle of preponderance of probability.

The ballistic expert, Sri Upen Borah, agreed with the post-mortem reports indicating the deceased died due to bullet injuries. He noted the short time frame for a grenade to explode and the improbability of no Army personnel being injured by grenade splinters.

The court notes that the army authorities' version of events is inconsistent with their own records and pleadings. For instance, the affidavit in opposition filed by the respondents No. 1 and 2 differs from the testimony of DW 1 regarding the apprehension of Pirush Warisa and Sujit Nunisa. These inconsistencies render the version of the army authorities unreliable.

The court notes that the army did not adhere to the norms as required under the law. It emphasizes the importance of involving civil authorities and the police in such operations and highlights the need to follow the 'Dos and Don'ts' list issued by the Army Headquarters.

The non-involvement of the police by the army personnel at the most crucial part of the operation, in the light of the aforesaid mandatory Dos and Don'ts, is incomprehensible. There is no reliable evidence to show that the deceased were involved with the activities of the extremist outfit.

The court considers the testimonies of PW1 to PW7 and the medical evidence from post-mortem reports. The court also notes the testimony of CW2, Sri Upen Bora, and the account of DW2 regarding the presence of 30 army personnel surrounding the two deceased persons.

The court notes that the operation was conducted during broad daylight, making it unlikely that the grenade and arms were found on the ground without being noticed by the surrounding army personnel. The court also considers the evidence of CW2, who stated that it is highly improbable that not a single army personnel was injured by the splinters on the blasting of the grenade.

The court observed that the army authorities had the burden and onus to prove that the recovery of arms and ammunitions were at the instance of the two deceased persons. The court noted that the police did not believe the version of the army as clearly mentioned in the status report submitted before the Court. The court found no reason not to accept the conclusion that hurling of grenade and firing by the two deceased is not believable.

The court notes that the contemporaneous medical report from Haflong Civil Hospital indicates a simple injury without any deep structure damage, contradicting the claim of a gunshot wound. The lack of mention of severe injury or loss of consciousness in earlier affidavits raises doubts about the authenticity of the claimed gunshot injury.

The burden of proving the circumstances under which the two persons died is on the army authorities, as the events are especially within their knowledge. The army authorities have failed to satisfactorily explain the death of the two persons in their custody and how they received multiple injuries over their bodies.

The court notes that the inquiry was focused and the army authorities had the opportunity to call additional witnesses but chose not to. The court finds that the army authorities failed to provide satisfactory explanations for the bruises on the deceased and the alleged injury of Yellappa Goudra. decision_text:
The Court allowed the petition and directed appropriate actions against the erring army personnel and awarded adequate compensation to the families of the deceased.

Taking into consideration the great harm done to the petitioner by the Government of Bihar, we are of the opinion that, as an interim measure, the State must pay to the petitioner a further sum of Rs 30,000 (Rupees thirty thousand) in addition to the sum of Rs 5000 (Rupees five thousand) already paid by it.

The Court has determined that there is no consistent view regarding the quantum of compensation for violation of fundamental rights, and there is a need for uniform principles to determine compensation amounts.

After taking into consideration the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the considered view that ends of justice will be met if the appellant is granted a sum of Rs.1,00,000.00 (Rupees one lakh only).

The payment was to be made by demand draft drawn in favor of the appellant 'Rohtash Kumar' within a period of one month from the date of the receipt of this order. The appeal is disposed of accordingly.
